source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current Java SE 26 ThreadPoolExecutor core/maximum/queue admission, rejection, hooks, keep-alive, monitoring, and shutdown plus ForkJoinPool behavior; Python 3.14.7 executor, future, deadlock, cancellation, and shutdown behavior; current Go pipeline cancellation guidance; and current Rayon work-stealing documentation were checked against official sources.

evidence: Reviewed worker W, active a, queue Q/capacity K, accepted A, terminal T, rejected R, lifecycle L, arrival/service/response quantities, work, and span.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Capacity/accounting invariants, queueing evidence, and performance heuristics remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed the two-worker three-slot six-submission schedule and independently confirmed 5 accepted, 1 rejected, queue high-water 3, maximum active 2, worker finish times 6 and 9, and makespan 9.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Exact counts match stdout under the stated ideal scheduling assumptions.

evidence: Re-derived accepted=queued+active+terminal preservation, fixed admission branches, same-pool child-future wait cycle, recursive-submission cycle, and graceful-termination reconciliation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Accounting does not imply deadlines, fairness, task correctness, or optimal sizing.

evidence: Reviewed zero queue capacity, unbounded queue, core/maximum interaction, worker creation failure, saturation, every rejection policy, same-pool dependency, recursive submit, task/hook failure, context leak, queued/running cancellation, resize, shutdown race, forced escalation, and stuck workers.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Every accepted identity reaches exactly one terminal disposition or is explicitly reported unresolved.

evidence: Checked worker/queue bounds, acceptance ownership, single queued/active/terminal states, byte/waiter/in-flight bounds, dependency acyclicity, context cleanup, cancellation arbitration, shutdown reject/drain/dispose/wake/join, and final reconciliation.
invariant_checking.notes: Approximate live metrics are never used as final completion authority.

evidence: Reviewed admission/accounting induction, Java queue-growth interaction, parent-child future deadlock, full-queue recursive submission, orderly shutdown, and caller-runs counterexamples.
proof_review.notes: Safety, liveness, overload feedback, cancellation, and performance are not conflated.

evidence: Audited the pool dependency diagram, sizing heuristic qualifications, finite schedule, executor API claims, shutdown semantics, and safety-critical boundary.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The wait-for diagram is explicitly non-executable and current API claims remain version-scoped.

evidence: Reproduced one executable Python arithmetic schedule and confirmed one schematic fence is intentionally skipped with a stated reason.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Evidence disclaims real threads, variable durations, scheduling cost, task dependencies, failures, cancellation, and general sizing/performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among pool, worker, queue, admission, rejection, direct handoff, work stealing, oversubscription, granularity, cancellation, and graceful/forced shutdown.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed CPU/blocking isolation, downstream limits, queue bytes/latency, rejection feedback, caller context, futures, recursive submission, task containment, context cleanup, cancellation, resizing, metrics, load tests, and shutdown.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter develops pools as bounded owned services from admission accounting through production tuning and termination using ten distinct examples and five progressively demanding matched exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, aerospace, medical, clinical, controls, hardware, real-time, functional-safety, cybersecurity, certification, regulatory, quality, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite arithmetic, source checking, and manual analysis do not prove production pool timing, fairness, task safety, optimal sizing, forced cancellation, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
